title: Implement 'useEffectEvent' / useEvent Polyfill
concept: Stable Identity Event Function with Always-Fresh Lexical Scope
problemStatement: Implement `useEffectEvent(handler)`: returns a function whose reference identity NEVER changes across renders, but when called, ALWAYS executes the latest `handler` passed on the most recent render.
interviewTrap: Developers often wrap handlers in `useCallback(fn, [deps])`, causing child components or effects to re-run whenever dependencies change. `useEffectEvent` extracts non-reactive event logic cleanly.

testCases.name: Stable function identity remains strictly identical across renders
testCases.testFn: const manager = createEffectEventManager(); const fn1 = manager.stableEvent; manager.updateHandler(() => 1); const fn2 = manager.stableEvent; return fn1 === fn2;

testCases.name: Executes the newest handler reading fresh props
testCases.input: handler updated with new prop value
testCases.testFn: const manager = createEffectEventManager(); manager.updateHandler((msg) => `${msg}: light`); manager.updateHandler((msg) => `${msg}: dark`); return manager.stableEvent('Theme');

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React's proposed `useEffectEvent` (formerly `useEvent`) polyfill extracts non-reactive event logic out of effects. It returns a stable function reference that can read the latest props and state without needing to be listed in the effect's dependency array, preventing unnecessary effect re-executions.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Maintain a mutable ref holding the latest callback: `const callbackRef = useRef(callback)`.
Use `useInsertionEffect` (or synchronous layout assignment) to update `callbackRef.current = callback` before effects run.
Return a stable wrapped function `useCallback((...args) => callbackRef.current(...args), [])` with empty dependencies.
When invoked inside an effect, the wrapper calls the freshest `callbackRef.current` without forcing the effect to re-run when callback dependencies change.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React RFC for `useEffectEvent`, the returned function is tagged as an Event function. React forbids calling Event functions during the Render phase, restricting their execution to Effects and Event Handlers. It separates reactive values (which must trigger effects) from non-reactive logic (which needs current values on demand).

complexity.space: O(1) ref and memoized callback allocation.

edgeCasesHandled: Effect does not re-trigger when callback's captured state changes.
Callback always has access to the most recent state and props.
Throws or warns if invoked during render phase.

specifications: React RFC: useEffectEvent (Separating Events from Effects)
React Official Docs: Separating Events from Effects with useEffectEvent
verifiedRules: Effect Events are not reactive and must not be included in effect dependencies.
Effect Events must only be invoked from within effects or event handlers, never during render.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is useEffectEvent (useEvent) and what architectural problem does it solve?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In React, effects often need to read current state/props to perform an action, but you do NOT want the effect to re-run whenever that state changes. `useEffectEvent` extracts non-reactive logic into an 'Effect Event' function. The returned function has a stable reference identity (can be omitted from effect dependencies), but always sees the freshest state when called inside an effect.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests knowledge of upcoming React 19 / official RFC hook architecture.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why must Effect Events NEVER be called during the render phase?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Effect Events read from mutable refs that update outside the pure render phase. Calling them during render breaks pure rendering rules and creates non-deterministic output in Concurrent Mode.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks understanding of React's strict purity boundaries.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Chat Room Analytics Logging on Connection
realWorldUseCases.description: Re-connecting to chat only when `roomId` changes, but logging the current `theme` without reconnecting when theme changes.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const onConnected = useEffectEvent(() => logConnection(theme)); useEffect(() => { connect(roomId); onConnected(); }, [roomId]);

howToExplain.opening: useEffectEvent separates reactive dependencies (which trigger effect re-runs) from non-reactive logic (which needs current values on demand).
keyPoints: Returns a stable function reference that never triggers effects.
Always accesses the freshest props and state when invoked.
Must only be called from inside effects or event handlers, never during render.
Solves the eternal dilemma of unnecessary effect re-executions.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Effect Events complete the hooks mental model by making non-reactive side effects first-class citizens in React.
analogies: An emergency contact card: you only change your wallet when you move homes (roomId), but when called, the contact reads your latest phone number (theme) without forcing you to buy a new wallet.

commonMistakes.mistake: Including useEffectEvent functions in useEffect dependency arrays.
commonMistakes.why: Effect Events are non-reactive by definition; React lint rules explicitly forbid listing them in dependencies.
commonMistakes.correct: Omit Effect Events from dependency arrays.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does useInsertionEffect help polyfill useEffectEvent?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `useInsertionEffect` runs synchronously before all layout effects and DOM mutations, updating the callback ref before any effect can possibly execute.
